preface.title: Preface
paragraphs: In this volume some of the subsidiary rites of the sacrifice (yajñāṅga-karma) are explained. A yajña is not a single rite. Many rites together make up the principal rite called yajña. In it there are many subsidiary rites, such as the milking of the cow (godohana), the churning of fire (agnimanthana), the bringing of the fire (agnyānayana), the bringing of the Soma (somapravāhaṇa), the Ātithyeṣṭi, the three pressings (savana) called Prātaḥsavana, Mādhyandinasavana and Tṛtīyasavana, and the Ṛtuyāja oblations. Of these, only the Ṛtuyāja oblations, the Somapravāhaṇa and the three pressings are explained in this volume.

In explaining such subsidiary rites of the sacrifice, they have to be explained from two points of view. For in every principal rite performed in sacrifices and the like there is a part for the priests called Hotṛ and Adhvaryu. The priests of the Hotṛ group recite, in the prescribed manner, the mantras suited to the rite concerned; the Adhvaryu, or the priests who assist the Adhvaryu, perform the actions suited to that rite. However small the actions performed in sacrifices may be, they must be carried out according to rule and with the recitation of mantras. Since the explanation of the actions, the procedure and so on belongs to the Adhvaryu group, and is given in the Yajurveda, the discussion of those matters has not been made here. But since the discussion of the mantras to be recited by the Hotṛ group in each rite belongs to the Ṛgveda,{{fn: The supplied text has ಋಗ್ವದಕ್ಕೆ ('Ṛgvada'), apparently for ಋಗ್ವೇದಕ್ಕೆ; the sense is the Ṛgveda.}} only the mantras to be recited by the Hotṛ group, when and how they are to be recited, and similar matters, are explained here, as stated in the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa. For all matters belonging to the Ṛgveda, such as the explanation of the mantra-procedures recited by the Hotṛ group, are stated in the two Brāhmaṇa works of the Ṛgveda, the Aitareya and the Kauṣītaki.

A Brāhmaṇa is a work that explains, for each important subsidiary rite and each principal rite performed in sacrifices and the like, the rule the Hotṛ is to follow, the mantra to be recited, the earlier history of that rite, why the rite is to be done, what fruit is obtained if it is done in a particular way, the fault that arises if it is not done according to rule, its expiation, and all such matters. Since the presentation of matters in the two Brāhmaṇas mentioned, the Aitareya and the Kauṣītaki, is more or less the same, and since in the southern country the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa is not particularly current while the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa is in use, we have explained everything concerning the Hotṛ in accordance with the Aitareya Brāhmaṇa.

Such a Ṛgveda-saṃhitā — most ancient, most profound, most extensive, and the root of all the śāstras — is not easy to publish in simple Kannada with a critical translation. Yet, with the weighty purpose that all people, scholars and laymen alike, may gain growth of knowledge through such a great undertaking and become worthy of the grace of God, His Highness Śrī Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar Bahadur, G.C.B., G.C.S.I., sovereign of the throne of Karnataka, lover of Vedic learning, himself a scholar, beloved of his people and devoted to God, and his Government, are encouraging the publication of this very costly work out of their generous patronage.{{fn: The supplied text has ಉದರಾಶ್ರಯದಿಂದ ('from the shelter of the stomach'), apparently a misreading of ಉದಾರಾಶ್ರಯದಿಂದ ('from generous patronage'); translated as 'generous patronage'.}} This must be called the good fortune of the people of Karnataka. I pray that the Lord of all, the Veda-puruṣa, may bestow upon such generous-minded Sovereign, upon his family, upon the Princess (who bears the mantra-name Gāyatrī, held to be the most important of the Vedic mantras), and upon all his subjects, all wealth — long life, health, prosperity and the other worldly fruits — and, to a still higher degree, spiritual knowledge that leads to the ultimate goal.
